title: California club scene and travel costs
summary: He talks about the Beverly Cabin closing, other California clubs, rail fare costs for the band and layoffs at airplane plants.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: And, uh, I think Joe Darinsburg is playing at some other place that this fellow opened up. It says quite a small place. It's not as big as the Beverly cabin, but, uh, they seem to be doing pretty good. The 400 is not open. Like they said, no, I think the 400 is open with Teddy Buckner. I think Teddy Buckner is back there. So, uh, I don't know what's what I, I haven't been writing out there for quite a while. Was a friend of ours, one of our fans I write to all the time. She always let me know, send me clippings of what's happening and all, you know. And so I'm gonna write to her one day this week and find out what's going on out there. Everybody want us out there, but, uh, the problem is to get a job somewhere else out there because that transportation problem was pretty tough on them fellas, you know what I mean, Bill? You see that, uh, take the band direct from here to, uh, California is a big price.
About a hundred and twenty dollars a piece for a railroad fare.

That's right. It's a big price, you see. So if they could, uh, combine about three or four different engagements out there like concerts or something like that, you know, and then we can go right on into the club after the concerts. It's finished like we did before. You see, but the way it is now, it's pretty tough. Cause a lot of them plants out there, airplane plants, are closed up. And that's a lot of people that's been laid off from work and they haven't been doing anything to be able to go to where it's going and where they have a good time like they want to.

So we just sitting back and waiting and hoping that's all we can do. And I just hope and trust the God that something will break in, huh? Even if we ever do have to go back across the water to work as long as it's working.
